docs.title: Match All Query
docs.text: The Match All Query returns all documents in the index. It's useful for browsing, getting total counts, or as a base for function scoring.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Get All Documents
docs.text:
// Retrieve all books (up to 100 by default)
ForageQueryResult<Book> results = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().buildForageQuery()
);

docs.title: With Limit
docs.text:
// Get first 10 documents
QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().buildForageQuery(10)

docs.title: With Sorting
docs.text:
// All documents sorted by rating
QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery()
    .buildForageQuery(100, Arrays.asList(
        new SortCriteria("rating", SortOrder.DESC)
    ))

docs.title: With Function Score
docs.text:
// All documents ranked by a field value
QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
    .fieldValueFactor("rating")
    .buildForageQuery(20)

docs.title: Browse All Items
docs.text:
// Product catalog browse
ForageQueryResult<Product> products = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery()
        .buildForageQuery(20, Arrays.asList(
            new SortCriteria("popularity", SortOrder.DESC)
        ))
);

docs.title: Filtered Browse
docs.text:
// All books in a category
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("category", "fiction")
        .clauseType(ClauseType.FILTER).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.MUST)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Count Total Documents
docs.text:
ForageQueryResult<Book> results = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().buildForageQuery(1)
);
long totalBooks = results.getTotal().getValue();

docs.title: Ranking Without Search Terms
docs.text:
// Show "top rated" without any search query
ForageQueryResult<Book> topRated = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
        .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
        .fieldValueFactor("rating")
        .buildForageQuery(10)
);

docs.title: Random Sampling
docs.text:
// Get random documents
ForageQueryResult<Book> random = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
        .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
        .scoreFunction(new RandomScoreFunction(System.currentTimeMillis(), "id_numeric"))
        .buildForageQuery(5)
);

docs.title: Scoring Behavior
docs.text:
Match All Query assigns a constant score of 1.0 to all documents:

// All documents get score = 1.0
QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().buildForageQuery()

This makes it ideal for function scoring where you want the score determined entirely by the function:

// Score = rating value (not multiplied by base score)
QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
    .fieldValueFactor("rating")  // Score comes entirely from rating
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: With Boosting
docs.text:
// Boost all matches (rarely needed)
QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery()
    .boost(2.0f)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Match All is very fast because it doesn't require term lookup:

Aspect Performance Query execution O(1) Result iteration O(n) where n = limit

Large Result Sets

Avoid requesting all documents at once for large indexes. Use pagination:

// Bad: potentially millions of results
QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().buildForageQuery(Integer.MAX_VALUE)

// Good: paginated
QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().buildForageQuery(20)

docs.title: Combining with Filters
docs.text:
Match All is often used as a base with filters:

// All books with rating >= 4.0
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("rating", 4.0f, 5.0f)
        .clauseType(ClauseType.FILTER).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.MUST)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Match Query
docs.text: The Match Query is the most fundamental query type. It searches for documents containing a specific term in a field.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java").buildForageQuery()

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. The search term is analyzed (tokenized, lowercased)
  2. Lucene searches the inverted index for matching terms
  3. Documents containing the term are returned with relevance scores
Search: "Java"
       ↓ (analysis)
Token: "java"
       ↓ (index lookup)
Matches: [doc1, doc5, doc12]

docs.title: Simple Match
docs.text:
// Find books with "effective" in the title
ForageQueryResult<Book> results = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "effective").buildForageQuery()
);

docs.title: Case Insensitive
docs.text:
Match queries are case-insensitive (due to standard analysis):

// All of these find the same documents
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java")
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "Java")
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "JAVA")

docs.title: With Boost
docs.text:
Increase the relevance weight of matches:

// Title matches are twice as important
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java")
    .boost(2.0f)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: With Result Limit
docs.text:
// Get top 5 matches
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "programming")
    .buildForageQuery(5)

docs.title: With Sorting
docs.text:
// Sort by score descending
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("author", "martin")
    .buildForageQuery(10, Arrays.asList(SortCriteria.byScore(SortOrder.DESC)))

docs.title: Field Types
docs.text: Match Query behavior depends on the field type:

docs.title: TextField (Analyzed)
docs.text:
// Document indexed with: new TextField("title", "Effective Java Programming")
// Tokens: ["effective", "java", "programming"]

QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java")        // ✓ Matches
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "effective")   // ✓ Matches
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "eff")         // ✗ No match (partial)
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "jav")         // ✗ No match (partial)

docs.title: StringField (Not Analyzed)
docs.text:
// Document indexed with: new StringField("isbn", "978-0134685991")
// Token: ["978-0134685991"]

QueryBuilder.matchQuery("isbn", "978-0134685991")  // ✓ Matches
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("isbn", "978")             // ✗ No match

docs.title: Multiple Terms
docs.text:
When searching for multiple terms, each term is matched separately:

// Searches for "clean" OR "code" (Lucene default)
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "clean code")

For exact phrase matching, use Phrase Query.

docs.title: Combining with Other Queries
docs.text:
// Match query as part of boolean query
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java").boost(2.0f).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("author", "bloch").build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Performance Considerations
docs.text: Factor Impact Common terms Slower (match many documents) Rare terms Faster (match few documents) Large fields Slightly slower Boosting Minimal overhead

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use specific fields: Search specific fields rather than a catch-all field when possible
  2. Limit results: Always specify a reasonable result limit
  3. Use boosting: Boost important fields to improve relevance

docs.title: Related Queries
docs.text:
• Fuzzy Query - Match with typo tolerance
  • Phrase Query - Match exact phrases
  • Prefix Query - Match prefixes
  • Boolean Query - Combine multiple match queries

docs.title: Phrase Query
docs.text: Phrase queries match documents containing an exact sequence of words.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "clean code").buildForageQuery()

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Unlike match queries that find any occurrence of terms, phrase queries require terms to appear in the exact order:

Document: "Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship"
          ↓ (tokenized)
Tokens:   ["clean", "code", "a", "handbook", "of", "agile", "software", "craftsmanship"]

Query: "clean code"
       ↓ (requires sequence)
Matches: Position 0: "clean", Position 1: "code" → ✓ Match!

Query: "code clean"
       ↓ (wrong order)
Result: ✗ No match

docs.title: Exact Phrase Match
docs.text:
// Find books with exact phrase "machine learning"
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "machine learning").buildForageQuery()

// Matches: "Machine Learning for Beginners"
// Matches: "Introduction to Machine Learning"
// No match: "Learning Machine Algorithms"

docs.title: Multi-Word Phrases
docs.text:
// Longer phrases
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "design patterns").buildForageQuery()
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("description", "object oriented programming").buildForageQuery()

docs.title: With Boost
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "clean code")
    .boost(2.0f)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Phrase vs Match Query
Phrase with Filters
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "design patterns").build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("rating", 4.0f, 5.0f).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.MUST)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Phrase OR Match (Flexible Search)
docs.text:
// Prefer phrase match, but allow individual term matches
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "clean code").boost(3.0f).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "clean").build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "code").build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Multi-Field Phrase Search
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "machine learning").boost(2.0f).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("description", "machine learning").build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Book/Article Titles
docs.text:
// Find exact book title
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "the pragmatic programmer")

docs.title: Technical Terms
docs.text:
// Multi-word technical terms
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("content", "dependency injection")
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("content", "test driven development")

docs.title: Quoted Search
docs.text:
// Implement quoted search like Google
String userQuery = "\"clean code\"";  // User typed with quotes

if (userQuery.startsWith("\"") && userQuery.endsWith("\"")) {
    String phrase = userQuery.substring(1, userQuery.length() - 1);
    query = QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", phrase);
} else {
    query = QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", userQuery);
}

docs.title: Analysis and Phrase Matching
docs.text:
Phrase queries work with analyzed text:

// Document: "The Quick Brown Fox"
// Analyzed tokens: ["the", "quick", "brown", "fox"]

// These all match:
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "quick brown")      // ✓
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "QUICK BROWN")      // ✓ (case-insensitive)
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "Quick Brown")      // ✓

// These don't match:
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "brown quick")      // ✗ (wrong order)
QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", "quick fox")        // ✗ (missing "brown")

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Phrase queries are efficient but slightly more expensive than simple match queries:

Aspect Impact Short phrases (2-3 words) Fast Long phrases (5+ words) Moderate Common first word Slightly slower

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Requires exact word sequence
  • No fuzzy matching within phrases
  • Stop words may be removed during analysis

docs.title: Prefix Query
docs.text: Prefix queries match documents where a field starts with a specified prefix. They're ideal for autocomplete functionality.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("author", "mart").buildForageQuery()
// Matches: "martin", "martinez", "martha", etc.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Index terms: ["martin", "martinez", "martha", "mark", "mary"]

Query prefix: "mart"
              ↓ (prefix expansion)
Matches: ["martin", "martinez", "martha"]

docs.title: Autocomplete
docs.text:
// User types "prog" in search box
String userInput = "prog";
QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", userInput).buildForageQuery()
// Matches: "programming", "progress", "program", "progressive"

docs.title: Author Name Autocomplete
docs.text:
// Find authors starting with "jo"
QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("author", "jo").buildForageQuery()
// Matches: "joshua bloch", "john doe", "jonathan swift"

docs.title: With Boost
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", "java")
    .boost(1.5f)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: With Result Limit
docs.text:
// Autocomplete suggestions (top 5)
QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", userInput)
    .buildForageQuery(5)

docs.title: Prefix with Filters
docs.text:
// Autocomplete within a category
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", "prog").build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("category", "technology")
        .clauseType(ClauseType.FILTER).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.MUST)
    .buildForageQuery(10)

docs.title: Multi-Field Prefix
docs.text:
// Search prefix in multiple fields
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", prefix).boost(2.0f).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("author", prefix).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Prefix OR Exact
docs.text:
// Boost exact matches higher than prefix matches
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", term).boost(3.0f).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", term).boost(1.0f).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Basic Autocomplete Endpoint
docs.text:
public List<String> autocomplete(String prefix, int limit) {
    ForageQueryResult<Book> results = engine.search(
        QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", prefix.toLowerCase())
            .buildForageQuery(limit)
    );

    return results.getMatchingResults().stream()
        .map(r -> r.getData().getTitle())
        .distinct()
        .collect(Collectors.toList());
}

docs.title: Autocomplete with Ranking
docs.text:
public List<String> autocomplete(String prefix, int limit) {
    // Rank by popularity/rating
    ForageQueryResult<Book> results = engine.search(
        QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
            .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", prefix).build())
            .fieldValueFactor("popularity")
            .buildForageQuery(limit)
    );

    return results.getMatchingResults().stream()
        .map(r -> r.getData().getTitle())
        .collect(Collectors.toList());
}

docs.title: Multi-Category Autocomplete
docs.text:
public Map<String, List<String>> autocomplete(String prefix) {
    Map<String, List<String>> suggestions = new HashMap<>();

    // Book titles
    suggestions.put("books", autocompleteField("title", prefix, 5));

    // Authors
    suggestions.put("authors", autocompleteField("author", prefix, 5));

    return suggestions;
}

private List<String> autocompleteField(String field, String prefix, int limit) {
    return engine.search(
        QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery(field, prefix).buildForageQuery(limit)
    ).getMatchingResults().stream()
        .map(r -> extractField(r.getData(), field))
        .distinct()
        .collect(Collectors.toList());
}

docs.title: TextField
docs.text:
Prefix matching works on individual tokens:

// Document: new TextField("title", "Java Programming Guide")
// Tokens: ["java", "programming", "guide"]

QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", "prog")  // ✓ Matches "programming"
QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", "java")  // ✓ Matches "java"
QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", "jav")   // ✓ Matches "java"

docs.title: StringField
docs.text:
Prefix matching works on the entire value:

// Document: new StringField("isbn", "978-0134685991")

QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("isbn", "978")     // ✓ Matches
QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("isbn", "978-01")  // ✓ Matches
QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("isbn", "0134")    // ✗ No match (not prefix)

docs.title: Performance Considerations
docs.text:
Factor Impact Short prefix (1-2 chars) Slow (many matches) Long prefix (4+ chars) Fast (fewer matches) Common prefix Slower

Short Prefixes

Very short prefixes (1-2 characters) can be expensive. Consider:

  • Requiring minimum prefix length (3+ chars)
  • Adding rate limiting
  • Caching common prefixes

docs.title: 1. Minimum Prefix Length
docs.text:
public List<String> autocomplete(String prefix) {
    if (prefix.length() < 3) {
        return Collections.emptyList();  // Require 3+ chars
    }
    // ... execute query
}

docs.title: 2. Debounce on Frontend
docs.text:
Wait for user to stop typing before sending request:

// Frontend debouncing
let timeout;
input.addEventListener('input', (e) => {
    clearTimeout(timeout);
    timeout = setTimeout(() => fetchSuggestions(e.target.value), 300);
});

docs.title: 3. Cache Results
docs.text:
private final Cache<String, List<String>> autocompleteCache =
    CacheBuilder.newBuilder()
        .maximumSize(1000)
        .expireAfterWrite(5, TimeUnit.MINUTES)
        .build();

public List<String> autocomplete(String prefix) {
    return autocompleteCache.get(prefix, () -> executeAutocomplete(prefix));
}

docs.title: Range Query
docs.text: Range queries filter documents based on numeric field values within a specified range.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
// Integer range
QueryBuilder.intRangeQuery("pages", 100, 500).buildForageQuery()

// Float range
QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("rating", 4.0f, 5.0f).buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Integer Range Query
docs.text:
// Books with 200-400 pages
QueryBuilder.intRangeQuery("pages", 200, 400).buildForageQuery()

// Books published after 2020
QueryBuilder.intRangeQuery("year", 2020, Integer.MAX_VALUE).buildForageQuery()

// Books published before 2020
QueryBuilder.intRangeQuery("year", Integer.MIN_VALUE, 2019).buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Float Range Query
docs.text:
// Books rated 4.0 to 5.0
QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("rating", 4.0f, 5.0f).buildForageQuery()

// Products under $50
QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("price", 0f, 49.99f).buildForageQuery()

// Products $100 and above
QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("price", 100f, Float.MAX_VALUE).buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Range Boundaries
docs.text:
Both boundaries are inclusive by default:

// Includes pages=100 and pages=500
QueryBuilder.intRangeQuery("pages", 100, 500)

// Document with pages=100 → ✓ Match
// Document with pages=300 → ✓ Match
// Document with pages=500 → ✓ Match
// Document with pages=501 → ✗ No match

docs.title: Range as Filter
docs.text:
// Search "programming" with rating filter
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "programming").build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("rating", 4.0f, 5.0f).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.MUST)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Multiple Range Filters
docs.text:
// Books: 200-500 pages, rating 4+, published 2020+
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.intRangeQuery("pages", 200, 500).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("rating", 4.0f, 5.0f).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.intRangeQuery("year", 2020, 2024).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.MUST)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Non-Scoring Filter
docs.text:
// Range filter that doesn't affect score
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java").build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("rating", 4.0f, 5.0f)
        .clauseType(ClauseType.FILTER).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.MUST)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: With Boosting
docs.text:
// Boost documents in the "sweet spot" page range
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "programming").build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.intRangeQuery("pages", 200, 400).boost(1.5f).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Field Requirements
docs.text:
Range queries require numeric fields:

// In your document creation
new ForageDocument(book.getId(), Arrays.asList(
    new IntField("pages", new int[]{book.getPages()}),     // ✓ Range queryable
    new IntField("year", new int[]{book.getYear()}),       // ✓ Range queryable
    new FloatField("rating", new float[]{book.getRating()}), // ✓ Range queryable
    new FloatField("price", new float[]{book.getPrice()})    // ✓ Range queryable
));

TextField Not Supported

Range queries don't work on TextField or StringField. Use IntField or FloatField.

docs.title: Price Filtering
docs.text:
// Products in price range
QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("price", minPrice, maxPrice)

docs.title: Date Range (as Epoch)

new IntField("publishedAt", new int[]{(int)(date.toEpochMilli() / 1000)})

// Query recent books (last 30 days)
long thirtyDaysAgo = Instant.now().minus(30, ChronoUnit.DAYS).getEpochSecond();
QueryBuilder.intRangeQuery("publishedAt", (int)thirtyDaysAgo, Integer.MAX_VALUE)

docs.text:
// Excellent: 4.5+
QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("rating", 4.5f, 5.0f)

// Good: 4.0-4.5
QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("rating", 4.0f, 4.49f)

// Average: 3.0-4.0
QueryBuilder.floatRangeQuery("rating", 3.0f, 3.99f)

docs.title: Quantity Filters

docs.title: Scoring & Ranking
docs.text: Forage provides powerful tools to control how search results are ranked. You can combine Lucene's relevance scoring with business signals to create the perfect ranking for your use case.

docs.title: Ranking Layers

    D -->|Sorting| E[Ordered Results]
    E -->|Minimum Score| F[Filtered Results]

docs.title: Ranking Components
docs.text: Component Purpose Documentation Query Boosts Emphasize specific query clauses Boost important fields Function Score Apply custom scoring functions Field values, scripts, decay Sorting Order results by criteria Score, field values Minimum Score Filter low-quality results Quality threshold

// Title matches are 2x more important than author matches
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()

    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)

docs.title: Scoring Modes
docs.text:
Function scores operate in two modes:

Mode Formula Use Case Multiplicative base_score × function_value Scale relevance by weight Direct Value function_value Replace score with field value 
// Multiplicative: WeightedScoreFunction, ScriptScoreFunction
// final_score = relevance_score × weight
QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java").build())
    .scoreFunction(new WeightedScoreFunction(2.0f))  // Score × 2

// Direct Value: FieldValueFactorFunction, ConstantScoreFunction
// final_score = field_value (ignores base relevance)
QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
    .fieldValueFactor("rating")  // Score = rating

docs.title: Function Score
docs.text: Function Score queries allow you to modify document scores using custom functions, field values, mathematical expressions, or decay functions.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java").build())
    .fieldValueFactor("rating")
    .buildForageQuery(10)

docs.title: Function Types
docs.text: Function Mode Score Calculation ConstantScoreFunction Direct score = constant WeightedScoreFunction Multiplicative score = base_score × weight FieldValueFactorFunction Direct score = field_value × factor ScriptScoreFunction Multiplicative score = base_score × expression_result RandomScoreFunction Direct score = random(seed, field) DecayFunction Direct score = decay(distance)

docs.title: Constant Score Function
docs.text:
Assigns a fixed score to all matching documents, ignoring the base query's relevance.

QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("category", "fiction").build())
    .constantScore(5.0f)  // All matches get score = 5.0
    .buildForageQuery()

Use case: When relevance doesn't matter, only matching does.

// All fiction books get the same score
var fictionBooks = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
        .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("category", "fiction").build())
        .constantScore(1.0f)
        .buildForageQuery(100)
);

docs.title: Weighted Score Function
docs.text:
Multiplies the base query score by a weight factor.

QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "programming").build())
    .scoreFunction(new WeightedScoreFunction(2.0f))  // Score × 2
    .buildForageQuery()

Use case: Scale relevance scores without changing ranking order.

// Double all scores (useful when combining with other scoring)
QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java").build())
    .scoreFunction(new WeightedScoreFunction(2.0f))
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Field Value Factor Function
docs.text:
Uses a numeric field's value as the score, optionally multiplied by a factor.

// Score = rating
QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
    .fieldValueFactor("rating")
    .buildForageQuery()

// Score = rating × 1.5
QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
    .fieldValueFactor("rating", 1.5f)
    .buildForageQuery()

Use case: Rank by a business metric (rating, popularity, sales).

// Top rated books
var topRated = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
        .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
        .fieldValueFactor("rating")
        .buildForageQuery(20)
);

// Results ordered: 4.9, 4.8, 4.7, 4.5, ...

docs.title: Script Score Function
docs.text:
Executes a JavaScript expression that can reference the base score and document fields.

// Score = base_relevance × rating
QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "programming").build())
    .scoreFunction(new ScriptScoreFunction("score * rating"))
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Available Variables
docs.text: Variable Description score Base query relevance score <fieldName> Any numeric DocValues field

docs.title: Expression Examples
docs.text:
// Blend relevance with rating
new ScriptScoreFunction("score * rating")

// Weighted combination
new ScriptScoreFunction("score * 0.7 + rating * 0.3")

// Complex formula
new ScriptScoreFunction("score * (1 + ln(popularity + 1))")

// Multiple fields
new ScriptScoreFunction("score * rating * freshness")

Use case: Create custom ranking formulas combining multiple signals.

// E-commerce: blend relevance, rating, and recency
var products = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
        .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("name", searchTerm).build())
        .scoreFunction(new ScriptScoreFunction("score * rating * recencyBoost"))
        .buildForageQuery(20)
);

docs.title: Random Score Function
docs.text:
Generates deterministic pseudo-random scores for consistent shuffling.

QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
    .scoreFunction(new RandomScoreFunction(
        42L,           // seed (same seed = same order)
        "id_numeric"   // field for randomization
    ))
    .buildForageQuery(10)

Use case: A/B testing, showing variety, avoiding bias.

// Show random selection to user (consistent per session)
long sessionSeed = session.getId().hashCode();
var randomPicks = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
        .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("category", "featured").build())
        .scoreFunction(new RandomScoreFunction(sessionSeed, "id_numeric"))
        .buildForageQuery(5)
);

docs.title: Decay Function
docs.text:
Scores decrease based on distance from an origin value. Three decay types available.

QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchAllQuery().build())
    .scoreFunction(new DecayFunction(
        origin,      // Optimal value (score = 1.0 at origin)
        scale,       // Distance at which score = decay
        offset,      // No decay within this distance
        decay,       // Score at scale distance (e.g., 0.5)
        decayType,   // GAUSS, EXP, or LINEAR
        field        // Numeric field name
    ))
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Decay Types
docs.text:
graph LR
    subgraph Decay Types
        A[GAUSS] -->|Bell curve| B[Smooth falloff]
        C[EXP] -->|Exponential| D[Rapid initial decay]
        E[LINEAR] -->|Straight line| F[Constant decay rate]
    end
Type Formula Character GAUSS Gaussian bell curve Smooth, natural falloff EXP Exponential decay Rapid initial drop LINEAR Linear decrease Constant rate

docs.title: Decay Examples
docs.text:
// Prefer books around 300 pages (± 50 pages is OK)
new DecayFunction(
    300.0,          // origin: ideal page count
    100.0,          // scale: score = 0.5 at 100 pages away
    50.0,           // offset: no decay within 50 pages
    0.5,            // decay: score at scale distance
    DecayType.GAUSS,
    "numPages"
)

// Prefer recent items (date as epoch seconds)
new DecayFunction(
    System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000.0,  // now
    86400 * 7,                             // scale: 7 days
    86400,                                 // offset: 1 day grace period
    0.5,
    DecayType.EXP,
    "publishedAt"
)

Use case: Location-based search, time-sensitive content, optimal value matching.

// Find medium-length books (prefer ~300 pages)
var mediumBooks = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
        .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("category", "programming").build())
        .scoreFunction(new DecayFunction(300.0, 100.0, 0.0, 0.5, DecayType.GAUSS, "numPages"))
        .buildForageQuery(10)
);

docs.title: Minimum Score
docs.text: Minimum score filtering removes low-quality results by setting a score threshold. Only documents with scores at or above the threshold are returned.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
// Only return results with score >= 0.5
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "programming")
    .buildForageQuery(10, null, 0.5f)

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Query Results:
  Doc1: score = 2.3  ✓ Returned
  Doc2: score = 1.8  ✓ Returned
  Doc3: score = 0.6  ✓ Returned
  Doc4: score = 0.4  ✗ Filtered (below 0.5)
  Doc5: score = 0.2  ✗ Filtered (below 0.5)

Minimum Score = 0.5
Returned: [Doc1, Doc2, Doc3]

docs.title: Basic Threshold
docs.text:
// Filter out weak matches
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java")
    .buildForageQuery(10, null, 0.5f)

docs.title: With Sorting
docs.text:
// Sort by score, minimum 0.3
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("content", searchTerm)
    .buildForageQuery(20, Arrays.asList(
        SortCriteria.byScore(SortOrder.DESC)
    ), 0.3f)

docs.title: With Function Score
docs.text:
// Custom scoring with threshold
QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "programming").build())
    .fieldValueFactor("rating")
    .buildForageQuery(10, Arrays.asList(
        SortCriteria.byScore(SortOrder.DESC)
    ), 2.0f)  // Minimum computed score of 2.0

docs.title: Quality Control
docs.text:
Filter out marginally relevant results:

// Only highly relevant matches
ForageQueryResult<Article> results = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.matchQuery("content", searchTerm)
        .buildForageQuery(20, null, 1.0f)
);

docs.title: Fuzzy Query Cleanup
docs.text:
Fuzzy queries can produce many weak matches:

// Filter out poor fuzzy matches
QueryBuilder.fuzzyMatchQuery("title", userInput)
    .buildForageQuery(10, null, 0.3f)

docs.title: Multi-Field Search
docs.text:
When searching across many fields, filter noise:

QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", term).boost(3.0f).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("author", term).boost(2.0f).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("description", term).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("tags", term).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery(20, null, 0.5f)  // Filter weak matches

docs.title: Relevance Guarantee
docs.text:
Ensure all results are truly relevant:

public ForageQueryResult<Book> search(String query) {
    return engine.search(
        QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", query)
            .buildForageQuery(10, Arrays.asList(
                SortCriteria.byScore(SortOrder.DESC)
            ), 0.5f)
    );
}

docs.title: Choosing Threshold Values
docs.text:
Threshold Behavior Use Case 0.0 No filtering Show all matches 0.1 - 0.3 Light filtering Remove very weak matches 0.3 - 0.5 Moderate filtering Quality-focused search 0.5 - 1.0 Aggressive filtering High precision required > 1.0 Very selective Only strong matches

Score Scales

Score values depend on your query type and data. Test with your actual data to find appropriate thresholds.

docs.title: Minimum Score + Pagination
docs.text:
// First page with quality filter
ForageQueryResult<Book> firstPage = engine.search(
    QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", searchTerm)
        .buildForageQuery(20, null, 0.5f)
);

// Pagination maintains the same filter
if (firstPage.getNextPage() != null) {
    ForageQueryResult<Book> nextPage = engine.search(
        new PageQuery(firstPage.getNextPage(), 20)
    );
}

docs.title: Dynamic Thresholds
docs.text:
Adjust threshold based on query type:

public ForageQueryResult<Book> search(String query, QueryType type) {
    float minScore = switch (type) {
        case FUZZY -> 0.3f;      // Lower for typo-tolerant
        case PHRASE -> 0.8f;     // Higher for exact phrases
        case BOOLEAN -> 0.5f;    // Moderate for combinations
        default -> 0.4f;
    };

    return engine.search(
        buildQuery(query, type)
            .buildForageQuery(20, null, minScore)
    );
}

docs.text:
Results: 100 documents
Scores range: 0.1 to 3.5
Average score: 0.8

docs.title: After Filtering (min = 0.5)
docs.text:
Results: 45 documents
Scores range: 0.5 to 3.5
Average score: 1.4

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Minimum score filtering is applied after the query executes:

  1. Query returns top N results
  2. Filter removes results below threshold
  3. Remaining results are returned

Result Count

If you request 20 results with a minimum score, you may get fewer than 20 if many are filtered out.

// May return 0-20 results depending on score distribution
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "obscure term")
    .buildForageQuery(20, null, 1.0f)

docs.title: Query Boosts
docs.text: Query boosts allow you to influence relevance by increasing or decreasing the importance of specific query clauses.

docs.title: Basic Concept
docs.text:
Boosting multiplies the score contribution of a query clause:

// Without boost: title match contributes score S
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java").build()

// With boost 2.0: title match contributes score S × 2
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java").boost(2.0f).build()

docs.title: Single Query Boost
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "programming")
    .boost(2.0f)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Boolean Query with Boosts
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java").boost(3.0f).build())   // 3x weight
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("author", "java").boost(2.0f).build())  // 2x weight
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("content", "java").boost(1.0f).build()) // 1x weight
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Nested Boolean with Boosts
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
        .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", searchTerm).build())
        .query(QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", searchTerm).boost(2.0f).build())
        .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
        .boost(3.0f)  // Boost entire title sub-query
        .build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("description", searchTerm).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Field Importance
docs.text:
Boost fields based on their relevance to search intent:

// For a book search
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", term).boost(5.0f).build())       // Most important
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("author", term).boost(3.0f).build())      // Very important
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("publisher", term).boost(1.5f).build())   // Somewhat important
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("description", term).boost(1.0f).build()) // Baseline
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Query Type Priority
docs.text:
Boost more specific queries higher:

// Prefer exact matches over partial matches
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", term).boost(3.0f).build()) // Exact phrase
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", term).boost(1.5f).build())        // Any word
    .query(QueryBuilder.prefixMatchQuery("title", term).boost(1.0f).build())  // Prefix
    .query(QueryBuilder.fuzzyMatchQuery("title", term).boost(0.5f).build())   // Fuzzy
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Recency Bias
docs.text:
Boost recent content (combine with date range):

int currentYear = Year.now().getValue();

QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", searchTerm).build())
    // Boost recent publications
    .query(QueryBuilder.intRangeQuery("year", currentYear - 1, currentYear)
        .boost(2.0f).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.intRangeQuery("year", currentYear - 3, currentYear - 2)
        .boost(1.5f).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: Boost Values
docs.text:
Boost Value Effect < 1.0 Reduces importance = 1.0 No change (default) > 1.0 Increases importance 
// Reduce importance
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("legacy_field", term).boost(0.5f)  // Half weight

// Increase importance
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", term).boost(2.0f)  // Double weight

// Significantly increase
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("exact_match", term).boost(5.0f)  // 5x weight

docs.title: Additive Effect (SHOULD)
docs.text:
With SHOULD, boosted clauses add to the total score:

// Document matching both: score = (title_score × 3) + (author_score × 2)
QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", term).boost(3.0f).build())
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("author", term).boost(2.0f).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)

docs.title: Required with Bonus (MUST + SHOULD)
docs.text:
Require some clauses, boost others:

QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
    // Required: must match title
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", term).build())
    // Bonus: author match boosts score
    .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("author", term).boost(2.0f)
        .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD).build())
    .clauseType(ClauseType.MUST)
    .buildForageQuery()

docs.title: E-Commerce Product Search
docs.text:
public ForageQuery buildProductQuery(String searchTerm) {
    return QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
        // Product name is most important
        .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("name", searchTerm).boost(5.0f).build())
        // Brand matches are valuable
        .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("brand", searchTerm).boost(3.0f).build())
        // Category context
        .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("category", searchTerm).boost(2.0f).build())
        // Description provides context
        .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("description", searchTerm).boost(1.0f).build())
        // SKU exact match (for power users)
        .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("sku", searchTerm).boost(10.0f).build())
        .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
        .buildForageQuery(20);
}

docs.title: Documentation Search
docs.text:
public ForageQuery buildDocsQuery(String searchTerm) {
    return QueryBuilder.booleanQuery()
        // Section title exact match
        .query(QueryBuilder.phraseMatchQuery("title", searchTerm).boost(10.0f).build())
        // Title contains words
        .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", searchTerm).boost(5.0f).build())
        // Code examples
        .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("code", searchTerm).boost(3.0f).build())
        // Body content
        .query(QueryBuilder.matchQuery("body", searchTerm).boost(1.0f).build())
        .clauseType(ClauseType.SHOULD)
        .buildForageQuery(15);
}

docs.text:
1. Start simple: Begin with default boosts, tune based on results
  2. Use relative values: Boost ratios matter more than absolute values
  3. Test with real queries: Verify ranking with actual search terms
  4. Document your boosts: Record why each boost was chosen

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text: Sorting controls the order in which search results are returned. You can sort by relevance score, field values, or a combination.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
// Sort by score (default)
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java")
    .buildForageQuery(10)

// Sort by field
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", "java")
    .buildForageQuery(10, Arrays.asList(
        new SortCriteria("rating", SortOrder.DESC)
    ))

docs.title: By Score
docs.text:
// Highest score first (default for most searches)
SortCriteria.byScore(SortOrder.DESC)

// Lowest score first (unusual, but available)

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text: Follow these best practices to build robust, performant search functionality with Forage.

docs.title: 1. Index Only What You Search
docs.text:
// Good: Minimal, purposeful fields
new ForageDocument(book.getId(), Arrays.asList(
    new TextField("title", book.getTitle()),
    new TextField("author", book.getAuthor()),
    new FloatField("rating", new float[]{book.getRating()})
));

// Avoid: Indexing everything
new ForageDocument(book.getId(), Arrays.asList(
    new TextField("title", book.getTitle()),
    new TextField("author", book.getAuthor()),
    new TextField("description", book.getDescription()),
    new TextField("tableOfContents", book.getToc()),      // Never searched
    new TextField("publisherNotes", book.getNotes()),     // Never searched
    new TextField("internalComments", book.getComments()) // Never searched
));

    new TextField("title", title),           // Full-text search
    new StringField("isbn", isbn),           // Exact match
    new StringField("status", status),       // Exact match

docs.title: 3. Handle Null Values
docs.text:
private ForageDocument createDocument(Book book) {
    List<Field> fields = new ArrayList<>();

    // Required fields
    fields.add(new TextField("title",
        book.getTitle() != null ? book.getTitle() : ""));

    // Optional fields - only add if present
    if (book.getDescription() != null && !book.getDescription().isEmpty()) {
        fields.add(new TextField("description", book.getDescription()));
    }

    // Numeric fields - use defaults for null
    fields.add(new FloatField("rating", new float[]{
        book.getRating() != null ? book.getRating() : 0.0f
    }));

    return new ForageDocument(book.getId(), fields);
}

    var results = engine.search(buildQuery(query));

@Override
public void bootstrap(Consumer<IndexableDocument> consumer) {
    int errors = 0;
    for (Book book : repository.findAll()) {

            consumer.accept(createDocument(book));
        } catch (Exception e) {
            errors++;
            log.error("Failed to index {}: {}", book.getId(), e.getMessage());

    }
    if (errors > 0) {
        log.warn("Bootstrap completed with {} errors", errors);

}

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text: This page covers frequently encountered issues and their solutions.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: Search returns empty results even though data exists.

docs.title: Possible Causes & Solutions
docs.text:
1. Bootstrap not completed 

// Ensure bootstrap completes before searching
updateEngine.bootstrap();
Thread.sleep(1000);  // Wait for indexing

// Or use proper synchronization
updateEngine.bootstrap();

2. Field name mismatch 

// Document indexed with "bookTitle"
new TextField("bookTitle", book.getTitle())

// But searching "title" - won't match!
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("title", searchTerm)  // Wrong field

// Fix: Use correct field name
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("bookTitle", searchTerm)  // Correct

3. Case sensitivity on StringField 

// StringField is case-sensitive
new StringField("category", "Technology")

// Won't match lowercase
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("category", "technology")  // No match

// Fix: Normalize during indexing
new StringField("category", book.getCategory().toLowerCase())

4. Using TextField for exact match 

// TextField tokenizes - "978-0134685991" becomes ["978", "0134685991"]
new TextField("isbn", book.getIsbn())

// Searching full ISBN won't work as expected
QueryBuilder.matchQuery("isbn", "978-0134685991")

// Fix: Use StringField for exact match
new StringField("isbn", book.getIsbn())

docs.text:

docs.text: Document scores show as NaN (Not a Number).

docs.title: Cause
docs.text:
Function score referencing missing or null field values.

// Document missing "rating" field
new ForageDocument(id, data, Arrays.asList(
    new TextField("title", title)
    // No rating field!
));

// Function score on missing field = NaN
QueryBuilder.functionScoreQuery()
    .baseQuery(...)
    .fieldValueFactor("rating")  // Field doesn't exist

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
Ensure all documents have the required fields:

new ForageDocument(id, data, Arrays.asList(
    new TextField("title", title),
    new FloatField("rating", new float[]{
        book.getRating() != null ? book.getRating() : 0.0f
    })
));

docs.title: Solutions

1. Handle exceptions in bootstrap 

@Override
public void bootstrap(Consumer<IndexableDocument> consumer) {
    for (Book book : repository.findAll()) {
        try {
            consumer.accept(createDocument(book));

}

        .collect(Collectors.toMap(

docs.title: Solution

Ensure Store returns correct types:

public Map<String, Book> get(List<String> ids) {
    return ids.stream()
        .filter(books::containsKey)
        .collect(Collectors.toMap(
            id -> id,
            id -> books.get(id)  // Correct Book type
        ));
